xref.title: Band Origin in Agoura Hills
xref.body: The core of Linkin Park began with three high school friends—Mike Shinoda, Brad Delson, and Rob Bourdon—who attended Agoura Hills High School, located approximately 30 miles northwest of downtown Los Angeles. "Everything with his band starts at a high school in Agora Hills, which is about 30 miles northwest of downtown Los Angeles."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Band's Stand Against Label Interference
xref.body: In an unusual move for a new band, Linkin Park directly met with Warner Brothers executives and firmly rejected various label suggestions, including demands to remove rapping, change Mike Shinoda's rap style to mimic Fred Durst, bring in a reggae vocalist named Matt Lyons, or introduce gimmicks for DJ Joe Hahn like wearing a cowboy hat and lab coat. They also refused to change their logo, which some at the label found "too Asian." "And the meeting was risky because new bands just don't show up in the boardrooms of major record labels and start dictating terms for how they were to be marketed and how their fan club should be treated."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Decreased Rap in Minutes to Midnight
xref.body: For their *Minutes to Midnight* album, the band intentionally reduced the amount of rap, with Mike Shinoda rapping on only two of the 12 songs. This decision was made because the "new metal" genre was perceived as "dead," and the band was uncertain about fan acceptance of rap in the evolving music landscape. "The new metal was dead so the amount of wrapping that fans might find acceptable was uncertain. So taking the safe route, they toned it down."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Early Band Formation
xref.body: Relative Degree was the first musical group in which Brad Delson and Rob Bourdon played together, preceding their formation of Super Zero with Mike Shinoda. "Brad and Rob were the first to play together in a group called Relative Degree."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Genre Evolution with Minutes to Midnight
xref.body: With "Minutes to Midnight," Linkin Park made a deliberate choice to shift their sound away from "pure new metal" into "a different sort of headspace." This change was partly evidenced by Mike Shinoda's increased singing roles and reduced rapping, appearing on only two of the album's 12 songs. "Lincoln Park made a conscious decision to move away from pure new metal into a different sort of headspace."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: On-Stage Headphones
xref.body: Brad Delson is known for wearing large, "clunky set of headphones" on stage, which were reportedly designed by Mike Shinoda. While Delson has never provided a direct explanation for wearing them, it is speculated they serve as monitors to ensure he can hear the band clearly during live performances. "Guitarist Brett Delson appears on stage wearing a big clunky set of headphones."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Precursor to Zero
xref.body: Super Zero was the band formed by Brad Delson, Rob Bourdon, and Mike Shinoda after their previous group, Relative Degree, disbanded. Its name was later shortened to "Zero" (spelled Xero). "When they broke up, they found Mike and Ford have called Super Zero, which was eventually shortened to just zero and spelled with an X, by the way."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Warner Brothers' Rap Suggestion
xref.body: Warner Brothers Records suggested that Mike Shinoda of Linkin Park should learn to rap in a style similar to Fred Durst. This was part of the label's efforts to influence Linkin Park's sound. "Mike should learn to wrap like Fred Durst."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Warner Brothers' Reggae Vocalist Suggestion
xref.body: During early discussions, Warner Brothers Records proposed bringing in a reggae vocalist named Matt Lyons to perform the rapping parts for Mike Shinoda in Linkin Park. This was one of several suggestions rejected by the band. "Or they could just bring in a reggae vocalist named Matt Lyons to do the wrapping for Mike."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
